junction.name: West 125 Street & Amsterdam Avenue, New York City

claims.text: West 125 Street & Amsterdam Avenue had 79 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 26 pedestrians injured, 24 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.4 million a year.
12% of crashes here involved a taxi or for-hire car, against 6% at the city's priority junctions.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.7 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites), worth $231,000 a year.
Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 4.3 crashes a year (CMF 4215, the median of 4 eligible records), worth $1.5 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for West 125 Street, Amsterdam Avenue (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 7, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 9.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 7, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 9
Subject: Request for safety study and signal timing fixes at West 125 Street & Amsterdam Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to request a safety study at the junction of West 125 Street & Amsterdam Avenue and action on the roads you are responsible for.

Official records for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 show 172 crashes, including 79 injury crashes. Pedestrians injured: 26. Cyclists injured: 24. People killed: 0. This location is a city priority location. The yearly cost of the harm, using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), is $5.4 million. No safety project is recorded in the period.

We ask you to consider:

* a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), expected to prevent 0.7 pedestrian injury crashes and $231,000 in harm per year. Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.
* longer yellow signal times, expected to prevent 4.3 injury crashes and $1,471,000 in harm per year, after checking on site for an entry on yellow or red.

Please assess feasibility, funding, and timing for these fixes on West 125 Street and Amsterdam Avenue.

Thank you for your work on street safety.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
